title: Numbers 10: How Old Are You? (год, года, лет)
titleRussian: Числа 10: сколько тебе лет? (год, года, лет)
description: All nine previous lessons brought to one daily question: how old are you? The word for 'year' has three forms - год, года, лет - and which one you use depends on the same rules you have been building. This is the synthesis lesson.
descriptionRussian: Все девять прошлых уроков сходятся в одном повседневном вопросе: сколько тебе лет? У слова 'год' три формы — год, года, лет, и выбор зависит от тех же правил. Это итоговый урок.
intro: Age is the most common thing you will be asked to say with a number, and it pulls the whole book together. The word for 'year' changes at exactly the borders you have been learning: one takes one form, two through four another, five and above a third. Only the last of those is a new word, and it is irregular.
rules: The Russian age frame is: [person in the dative] + [number] + [year form]. Example: Маше двадцать пять лет.
Год (the dictionary form) is used after numbers whose last word is 1: один год, двадцать один год.
Года (gen sg) is used after numbers whose last word is 2, 3, or 4, not part of a teen: два года, двадцать четыре года.
Лет (irregular gen pl) is used after 5-20, teens (11-19), and round tens (20, 30, ... 100): пять лет, тринадцать лет, сорок лет.
Лет is the only new memorisation. It comes historically from лето ('summer'); native speakers treat it as a fixed counting form.
examples: Маше один год. (Masha is one year old.) Last word 1: agreement → год.
Антону два года. (Anton is 2.) Last word 2: gen sg → года.
Лене три года. (Lena is 3.) Last word 3: gen sg → года.
Соне пять лет. (Sonya is 5.) 5+: gen pl → лет.
Маше тринадцать лет. (Masha is 13.) Teen: gen pl → лет.
Антону двадцать один год. (Anton is 21.) Last word 1: agreement → год.

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lesson 9: I have twenty books.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 9. A round ten takes the genitive plural: книг. Today, the same family of rules picks the form of 'year'.

items.hint: Last word 3 → gen sg of year.
items.explanation: After the number 3 the noun takes the genitive singular: года. The Russian frame is 'Лене (dative) + три + года'. Same machinery as 'три брата', applied to the word 'year'.
After 'пять' the noun takes the genitive plural: лет. The form is irregular - it comes historically from 'лето' rather than from 'год'. In age contexts, лет is always the answer for 5+.

items.hint: Last word is один - agreement rule.
items.explanation: В составном числе 21 последнее слово — 'один'. Это правило согласования (Lesson 2): год остаётся в словарной форме. The English 'twenty-one years old' may feel plural, but Russian sticks to the singular agreement form год.
Тринадцать is a teen (11-19), and teens always take the gen pl, regardless of what the second digit looks like. Тринадцать лет, четырнадцать лет, пятнадцать лет: all лет.

items.promptEnglish: Lena is one hundred years old.
items.hint: Round ten / 100 → gen pl of year.
items.explanation: Сто ведёт себя как круглый десяток. The gen pl лет is used after round tens just as it is after 5-20 and the teens. Сто лет is the standard phrase for 'a hundred years'; you will see it in idioms and birthday wishes.

blanks: Маше двенадцать _____. (Masha is twelve years old.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 12 is a teen; teens always take the gen pl form of year - лет. Despite the visible '2' in '12', the teens are one fused counting group with the 5+ rule.

errorCorrection.explanation: Compound numbers follow the rule of the LAST digit. Двадцать один ends in 'один' (1), and numbers ending in 1 (except 11) take год (nominative singular). Лет belongs to 5+ and the teens, so it cannot follow 21.

Numbers ending in 2, 3, or 4 (except the teens 12-14) take года (gen sg). Три → года: 'Маше три года' ('Masha is 3'). Лет is for 5+ and the teens, so it does not fit три. The age construction also uses dative on the person (Маше, not Маша); that's a separate rule covered in the dative track.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena turned five years old yesterday.
errorCorrection.explanation: Numbers ending in 5 through 9, 0, AND the teens 11-14 all take лет (gen pl): 'Лене пять лет'. Год is the form for numbers ending in 1, so it cannot follow пять. The full pattern: 1-ending → год, 2/3/4-ending (not 12/13/14) → года, everything else → лет. The teens 11-14 break the apparent pattern and join the лет group; that's the most-missed corner of the rule.

minimalPairs.explanation: Last word один → agreement → год. The teen reflex ('it ends in 1, so it must be...No wait, 21 is not a teen, so the last-word rule applies') is exactly the diagnostic this lesson trains.
12 is a teen; teens always take лет, regardless of the second digit. The form года would only fit non-teen numbers ending in 2, 3, or 4 (двадцать два года, тридцать четыре года).

patternRecognition.question: Which rule applies?
patternRecognition.explanation: После 'один' существительное стоит в словарной форме (правило согласования из Lesson 2). The noun год does not change. Same rule that produces один брат produces один год.

patternRecognition.question: Which rule applies?
patternRecognition.explanation: After 'три' the noun takes the genitive singular (the 2-3-4 rule from Lessons 4-6). Год → года. Same rule that produces три брата produces три года.

patternRecognition.question: Which rule applies?
patternRecognition.explanation: Пятнадцать is a teen (11-19), and teens always take the gen pl (Lesson 8). Year → лет (irregular gen pl). Same family as пять лет, двадцать лет, сто лет.

patternRecognition.question: Which rule applies?
patternRecognition.explanation: Сто ведёт себя как круглый десяток (Lesson 9). Year → лет. The phrase 'сто лет' is also a common idiom: 'я тебя сто лет не видела' ('I have not seen you in ages').

reviewVocab.definition: age (framed in Russian as dative + number + year form)
reviewVocab.example: В вопросе 'Сколько Маше лет?' речь идёт о возрасте: дательный 'Маше' + вопросительное 'сколько' + форма 'лет'.

reviewVocab.definition: irregular gen pl of год; used after 5-20, teens, and round tens; from лето ('summer')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маше двадцать пять лет' слово 'лет' — нерегулярная форма родительного падежа множественного числа от слова 'год'.

reviewVocab.definition: dative experiencer (the dative form of the person whose age is being given; introduced fully in the A2 Dative track)
reviewVocab.example: В выражении 'Антону тридцать лет' слово 'Антону' — дательный субъекта: тот, чей возраст называется.
